senses.gloss: (b. h.) to rest, lie; to be at ease, rest satisfied.—
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 7b:8-9">Sabb. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>זרק … והלכה ונָחָה וכ׳</he> if one threw an object higher than ten handbreadths, and in its course it came to rest in a little hole.
<cite ref="Shabbat 7b:10">Ib.</cite> <he>וזרק ונָח על גביו</he> and he threw an object and it came to rest on it.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 25:2">Gen. R. s. 25</cite> <he>כיון שעמד נֹחַ נָחוּ</he> when Noah rose, they rested (submitted to man’s rulership; Yalk. Chr. 1072 <he>נִינּוֹחוּ</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 42:3">Yalk. Gen. 42</cite> <cite ref="N00510"><he>נִחֲמָן</he></cite> he appeased them); <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 42:3">ib.</cite> <he>וכיון שעמד נֹחַ נחו</he> and when Noah rose, they remained undisturbed in their graves; Yalk. Chr. l. c. <he>נינוחו</he>.—
<cite ref="Megillah 25b">Meg. 25ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>יָנוּחוּ לו ברכות וכ׳</he> blessings rest upon his head.

<cite ref="Shabbat 152b">Sabb. 152ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>תָּנוּחַ … שהנחת וכ׳</he> let thy mind be at rest, for thou hast set my mind at rest; a. fr.—Part. <cite ref="N00468"><he>נָח</he></cite>, <cite ref="N00342"><he>נוֹחַ</he></cite>, f. <cite ref="N00343"><he>נוֹחָה</he></cite>; pl. <he>נוֹחִים</he>, <he>נוֹחִין</he>; <he>נוֹחוֹת</he>
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 11:5">Gen. R. s. 11</cite> <he>אתם נוחין</he> you rest.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 3:9:3">Y. Erub. III, end, 21ᶜ</cite>, a. fr. <he>נוֹחֵי נפש</he> whose souls are at rest; a. fr.—
senses.label: a

units: <cite ref="Pirkei Avot 3:10">Ab. III, 10</cite> <he>כל שרוח הבריות נ׳ הימנו וכ׳</he> in whom the mind of man finds pleasure, the mind of God finds pleasure.
<cite ref="Mishnah Sheviit 10:9">Shebi. X, 9</cite>; a. fr.—V. <cite ref="N00342"><he>נוֹחַ</he></cite>.
senses.label: b

senses.gloss: to set at rest; to set down, place. Gen. R. l. c. (ref. to Gen. V, 29) או נח זה יְנִיחֵנוּ וכ׳ either let him be called Noaḥ, then it ought to read, ‘he shall set us at rest’, or Naḥman &c. Sabb. l. c. שהֵנַחְתָּ, v. supra; (Snh. 30ᵇ שהתנחת, v. תָּנַח; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 20).
units: <cite ref="Chullin 91b:8">Ḥull. 91ᵇ</cite> <he>עלי יַנִּיחַ צדיק וכ׳</he> let this righteous man rest his head on me.—
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Kamma 3:1">B. Kam. III, 1</cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 6:6">B. Mets. VI, 6</cite> <he>הַנַּח לפני</he> put it down before me (I will take charge of it).
<cite ref="Shabbat 21b:8">Sabb. 21ᵇ</cite> <he>להַנִּיחָהּ על פתח וכ׳</he> to place it over the entrance &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to leave; to leave alone; to allow.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 9:1">B. Bath. IX, 1</cite> <he>מי שמת וה׳ בנים וכ׳</he> if a person died and left sons and daughters.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 9:3">Ib. 3</cite> <he>ראו מה שה׳ לנו וכ׳</he> see what our father left us.
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 30a">Snh. 30ᵃ</cite> <he>מעות שה׳ לו אביו</he> money which his father had left him (without telling him where it was deposited).
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 26">Pesik. R. s. 26</cite>; Yalk. Ps. 884 <he>אבינו ירמיה הרי אתה מַנִּיחֵנוּ שם</he> J., our father, wilt thou leave us there (in Babylonia, without a prophet)?—
<cite ref="Beitzah 30a">Bets. 30ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>הַנַּח להם לישראל</he> leave Israel alone (let them do as they please).
<cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 1:4">Yoma I, 4</cite> <he>לא היו מְנִיחִים אותו וכ׳</he> they did not let him eat much.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 10b:12">Ab. Zar. 10ᵇ</cite> <he>יַנִּיחֶנָּה</he>, v. <cite ref="N00372"><he>נוֹמִי</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 17a">Ib. 17ᵃ</cite> <he>לא ה׳ זונה וכ׳</he> he did not forego a single prostitute &c.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 30:15">Ex. R. s. 30</cite> <he>לא ה׳ שלא היה מצערו</he> he allowed no opportunity to pass without tormenting him; a. v. fr.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 13a">Ab. Zar. 13ᵃ</cite> <he>יום שע״א מֵנַחַת בו וכ׳</he> a day on which the idol grants a remission of duties.
<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 13a:2">Ib.</cite> <he>כל מי … ויָנִיחַ … יָנִיחַ וכ׳</he> to him who will take a wreath and place it on his head (in honor of the deity), he will allow a remission &c.; a. fr.

senses.gloss: to wish rest (to a deceased); to bless the memory of.
units: Yalk. Ex. 411 מזכירין ומניחין there are those who are mentioned and blessed (opp. משחקין); Ex. R. s. 48 מדכרין ומניחין; (Tanḥ. Vayakh. 4 מזכירין ומשבחים;) [Midr. Sam. ch. I מדכרין ומניחין we mention and let alone, neither praising nor blaming by mentioning the ancestry].
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 16:5">Gen. R. s. 16</cite> <he>לַהֲנִיחוֹ וכ׳</he> to give him pleasure, to protect him &c.

<cite ref="Shabbat 4a">Sabb. 4ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>קלוטה כמי שהוּנְחָה דמיא</he> an object intercepted in the air (crossing an area, v. <cite ref="T01079"><he>רָשׁוּת</he></cite>) is considered as having rested there, v. <cite ref="E00673"><he>הַנָּחָה</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Metzia 3:4">B. Mets. III, 4</cite>, a. e. <he>יהא מוּנָח וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="A01840"><he>אֵלִיָּהוּ</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Yoma 72b:6">Yoma 72ᵇ</cite> <he>עדיין מונח הוא וכ׳</he> still lies (undisposed of), whosoever desires to obtain it &c.
<cite ref="Kiddushin 66a:11">Kidd. 66ᵃ</cite> <he>הרי כרוכה ומוּנַחַת וכ׳</he> it (the Law) is wrapped up and lies in the corner, whosoever wishes to study &c.; a. fr.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:5">Cant. R. to VII, 5</cite> <he>והגליות באות ונִינּוֹחוֹת וכ׳</he> and the exiles will come and rest under it; (<cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 334">Yalk. Is. 334</cite> <he>ונוֹחוֹת</he>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 575:1">Yalk. Zech. 575</cite> <he>וחָנוֹת</he>). Y. Ber. V, end, 9ᵈ <he>בטוח אני שנ׳ בנו וכ׳</he> I am confident that the son of … will recover from his illness.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 13">Gen. R. s. 13</cite> <he>נִינּוֹחוּ</he> they are relieved (out of danger). Yalk. Chr. 1072, v. supra; a. e.
